items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: Jack Lane played trap drums. Now, he had a complete set of drums... That was one way organized the Reader Alliance band.

ctx.x: Do you remember any of the tunes your father played on the harmonica?

Oh, yeah. All them old tunes. Swanee River. And I only just wanted to know. Widow done. Six Little Angels. Boy, we're going back now. We're going back now. We used to play that Long Sonata. Oh, yeah? Yeah, Long Sonata used to, because you see, he knew it. And I knew it. And when we played, we had with Jack Lane, Jack Lane to make all kind of four faces. Man, he'd be making faces a day, you know, and Mark McCurt sitting on the side of me. He'd be laughing or just Long Sonata, guitar and the string bass player that…
How many brothers did you have? Three. Did they all play music?

items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: Popeye Lane's living, he'll tell you. We used to play that soft...

ctx.x: Well, that generation is forgotten today, pretty much. I know.

I know, but today, the generation and the musicians that they have now will never, and you can take that from me as an authority, will never play the music we used to play in our days. For the simple reason is that they didn't, they gave you a program. All right, you play according to the program. Now, that program maybe might have contained 12, 14, or 16 different type dances. Mazzucca, lances, shatters, waltzes, minuets, varieties. That was all on the program, and you played just the way the program was. Show…
Yeah, I'm gonna get a cigarette. Uh, I was wondering something. How did you get your start in music?
